definitions.explanation: A physical or figurative wall that blocks progress or separates things. Used for trade barriers, language barriers, social obstacles, and literal walls or partitions.

examples.japanese: {言葉|ことば}の{障壁|しょうへき}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}える。
{関税|かんぜい}は{貿易|ぼうえき}の{障壁|しょうへき}となっている。
examples.english: Tariffs have become a barrier to trade.

examples.japanese: {新規|しんき}{参入|さんにゅう}を{妨|さまた}げる{障壁|しょうへき}を{取|と}り{除|のぞ}くことが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: It is necessary to remove barriers that prevent new entrants.

notes:
Compound of {障|しょう} (to obstruct) + {壁|へき} (wall). Used in both concrete and abstract senses.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {障壁|しょうへき}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}える (to overcome a barrier)
- {障壁|しょうへき}を{取|と}り{除|のぞ}く (to remove a barrier)
- {言葉|ことば}の{障壁|しょうへき} (language barrier)
- {貿易|ぼうえき}{障壁|しょうへき} (trade barrier)
- {心理的|しんりてき}{障壁|しょうへき} (psychological barrier)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{壁|かべ} (wall) is more colloquial and can also mean "barrier" figuratively. {障壁|しょうへき} is more formal and tends to appear in written or official contexts. {障害|しょうがい} (obstacle/impediment) is broader and includes non-wall-like hindrances.
